 Follow Tony Gilroy suggests we "blow up the AI centers" at the voting box. At the voting box!
 Matt Schimkowitz Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:35 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Andor fans should be familiar with Tony Gilroy's not-so-subtle injection of real politics into the Star Wars galaxy. Gilroy is no stranger to artfully discussing fascism, exploitation, and dehumanization through the lens of Galactic Empires and Kyber Crystals. But when it comes to promotional tours for his upcoming cello drama Behemoth! , Gilroy is happy to make the subtext text. Gilroy appeared alongside his Behemoth! star Pedro Pascal at Vanity Fair 's Screen Talk event last weekend . Towards the end of the event, moderator John Ross, Vanity Fair 's West Coast editor, wondered what AI would do to entertainment and how humanity might push back. Pascal warmed up the crowd with an optimistic vision. "There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling," Pascal said. "We want to be human beings, and we want to be connected to one another, and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope." Gilroy had a different take: "Blow up the AI centers, man." 
 Now, as much as we all love to see the Michael Clayton maestro advocating for "terrorism" (as a nervous Pascal describes it), we feel compelled to note that Gilroy was speaking euphemistically, using an expression no one has ever heard or used before. "I don't mean blow them up, like blow them up. I mean, like, blow them up at the voting box," he clarified. Perhaps sensing that articles like this one were coming down the pike, Gilroy pivoted to plugging Alex Gibney's documentary Musk . "Go vote and blow them up. But man, go see the Musk documentary, man. Watch all four hours. I'm pitching my movie, but watch that movie." Gilroy, man, then returns to the initial discussion on the future of entertainment. "Maybe we'll all end up in regional theater. I have a fantasy where it's regional theater with multiple episodes, but the episodes go from New York to Chicago, and you like… I'm going out with humans."
 So, what we have gathered: The expression "blow up AI centers" is a call for a new entertainment ecosystem in which episodic regional theater productions tour the countryside as blown-out data centers smoulder from sea to shining sea, man.
